page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a narrow marginal note at the right margin beside the upper part of the column ("Turca"), a second marginal note at the right beside the middle ("Sophi"); a signature mark at the foot centred below the last line.

main_text.p: constructis: ex quibus præcipua est Samar- canda, quam jaxartes, maximus Sogdianæ fluvius,interluit; qui & in mare Caspium se exonerat. Hujus conditor Tamerlanus fuis- se dicitur:cum quibus dum Sophi rex Persa Turca-rum bellum nostrâ gereret ætate, à Selymo Turcarum Imperatore invasus & victus est: qui & illi quicquid in Armenia possidebat, unà cum Taurifio regni capite ademit, Bi- libaldus Pirkermerus. Non ignorandum, Sophiinquit idem,eam gentem, quæ hodie Tur- carum appellatur nomine, à Tartaris ortum sumpsisse, quòd non solum una & eadem lingua,ritus,victus & vestitus, sed & equitandi ac bellandi usus, nec non fraudes, perfidia & innata barbaries ostendit & feri- tas.Falluntur igitur, qui Turcarum gentem antiquissimam, aut Turcimanos esse putant: cùm paruo plus sint,quàm trecenti anni,ex quo primùm Tartarorum nomen,antea pe- nitus incognitū,sit auditum: post quorum ad- ventum Ottomannus se à Tartaris sejunxit, ac cum suis Turcarum nomen assumpsit. Tartarique hodierna die Turcas clientes suos esse dicunt, ac Deum ob peccata eorum, Turcas sic extul se conqueruntur: quum antea non solùm illorum fuerint subditi, sed rustici etiam s idq; Turcarum nomine signi-

page.notes: Marginal notes read "Turca-" (beside "Turcarum", line 7 of the column, right margin) and "Sophi" (beside "Non ignorandum", right margin); the second is printed in a small italic/heavy face and partly smudged. Several words are faint or smudged on the scan, notably "Samarcanda"/"Sogdianæ" in the first lines and "signi-" at the foot; a few letters are uncertain (e.g. "paruo" read as printed, "Taurifio"); the left and lower edges show stains. Hyphenated line-end "Turca-" / "feri-" / "pe-" / "ad-" are kept as printed; the catchword/signature line "K 4" is set at the foot below the final line and is recorded as a signature. Where the scan is too faint to read with certainty, the reading above is the best available and should be checked against the original.
